title: “Stranger on the Shore” by Acker Bilk
text: "Stranger on the Shore" is a piece for clarinet written by Acker Bilk for his young daughter and originally named "Jenny" after her. The tune was written on a single scrap of paper by Bilk and handed over to arranger Leon Young who crafted the string arrangement, including the characteristic harmonic shifts at the very end.
listen: Stranger on the Shore Acker Bilk

title: “I Can't Stop Loving You” by Ray Charles
text: "I Can't Stop Loving You" is a popular song written and composed by country musician Don Gibson from his 1958 album Oh Lonesome Me, who first recorded it on December 3, 1957, for RCA Victor Records. It was released in 1958 as the B-side of "Oh Lonesome Me", becoming a double-sided country hit single.
listen: I Can't Stop Loving You Ray Charles

title: “Mashed Potato Time” by Dee Dee Sharp
text: "Mashed Potato Time" is a song recorded by American R&B singer Dee Dee Sharp and released in 1962 by Cameo-Parkway Records. Written by Kal Mann and produced by Bernie Lowe, the song was inspired by the Mashed Potato dance craze of the early 1960s.
listen: Mashed Potato Time Dee Dee Sharp

title: “Roses Are Red (My Love)” by Bobby Vinton
text: "Roses Are Red" is a popular song composed by Al Byron and Paul Evans. It was recorded by Bobby Vinton, backed by Robert Mersey and his Orchestra, in New York City in February 1962, and released in April 1962, and the song was his first hit.
listen: Roses Are Red (My Love) Bobby Vinton

title: “The Stripper” by David Rose
text: "The Stripper" is an instrumental composed by David Rose, recorded in 1958 and released four years later. It evinces a jazz influence with especially prominent trombone slides, and evokes the feel of music used to accompany striptease artists.

title: “Johnny Angel” by Shelley Fabares
text: "Johnny Angel" is a song written and composed by Lyn Duddy and Lee Pockriss. It was originally recorded by both Laurie Loman and Georgia Lee, but those two versions were not successful.

title: “The Loco-Motion” by Little Eva
text: "The Loco-Motion" is a pop song written by American songwriters Gerry Goffin and Carole King. It was originally written for R&B singer Dee Dee Sharp, but she turned the song down.

title: “Let Me In” by The Sensations
text: "Let Me In" is the name of a 1961 song with music and lyrics by Yvonne Baker, recorded the same year by Baker and The Sensations, which went to No. 2 on the US R&B singles chart and No.

title: “The Twist” by Chubby Checker
text: "The Twist" is an American song written and originally released in 1958 by Hank Ballard and the Midnighters as a B-side to "Teardrops on Your Letter". It was inspired by the twist dance craze.

title: “Soldier Boy” by The Shirelles
text: "Soldier Boy" is a song written by Luther Dixon and Florence Greenberg and made famous by the girl group the Shirelles. Released as a single in 1962, it met with great success, topping the US Billboard Hot 100 for three consecutive weeks.

title: “Hey! Baby” by Bruce Channel
text: "Hey! Baby" is a song written by Margaret Cobb and Bruce Channel, recorded at Clifford Herring Studios in Fort Worth, Texas, by Channel in 1961.

title: “The Wanderer” by Dion
text: "The Wanderer" is a song written by Ernie Maresca and originally recorded by Dion, released on his 1961 album, Runaround Sue. The song, with a 12-bar blues-base verse and an eight-bar bridge, tells the story of a travelling man and his many loves.

title: “Duke of Earl” by Gene Chandler
text: "Duke of Earl" is a 1962 US number-one song, originally recorded by Gene Chandler. It is the best known of Chandler's songs, and he subsequently dubbed himself "The Duke of Earl".

title: “Palisades Park” by Freddy Cannon
text: "Palisades Park" is a song written by Chuck Barris and recorded by Freddy Cannon.

title: “Breaking Up Is Hard to Do” by Neil Sedaka
text: "Breaking Up Is Hard to Do" is a song recorded by Neil Sedaka, co-written by Sedaka and Howard Greenfield. Sedaka recorded this song twice, in 1962 and 1975, in two significantly different arrangements, and it is considered to be his signature song.
wiki: Breaking Up Is Hard to Do
listen: Breaking Up Is Hard to Do Neil Sedaka

title: “Wolverton Mountain” by Claude King
text: "Wolverton Mountain" is a country music song and 1962 crossover hit that established Claude King's career as an American country singer-songwriter. The song was a cover of the original version by Merle Kilgore, which was based on a real person named Clifton Clowers.

title: “Slow Twistin'” by Chubby Checker & Dee Dee Sharp
text: "Slow Twistin'" is a song recorded by American singers Chubby Checker and Dee Dee Sharp, released in 1962 by Parkway Records. Written by Kal Mann and Dave Appell, the song was produced by Bernie Lowe and became a hit on the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at No.
listen: Slow Twistin' Chubby Checker & Dee Dee Sharp

title: “It Keeps Right On a-Hurtin'” by Johnny Tillotson
text: "It Keeps Right On a-Hurtin'" is a song written and recorded by Johnny Tillotson, which was a major hit for him in 1962. The song was nominated for a Grammy for Best Country & Western song for 1962 but lost to Burl Ives' "Funny Way of Laughing".
listen: It Keeps Right On a-Hurtin' Johnny Tillotson

title: “The One Who Really Loves You” by Mary Wells
text: "The One Who Really Loves You" is a single recorded by Mary Wells on the Motown label in 1962 and released on her album of the same name. It was written and composed by Smokey Robinson of The Miracles and peaked at number eight on the Billboard Hot 100 chart and number two on the Billboard R&B chart.
wiki: The One Who Really Loves You (song)
listen: The One Who Really Loves You Mary Wells

title: “Good Luck Charm” by Elvis Presley
text: "Good Luck Charm" is a song recorded by Elvis Presley and published by Gladys Music, Elvis Presley's publishing company, that reached number 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 list in the week ending April 21, 1962. It remained at the top of the list for two weeks.

title: “Midnight in Moscow” by Kenny Ball
text: "Moscow Nights", originally titled "Leningrad Nights", is a Soviet patriotic song written by Mikhail Matusovsky and composed by Vasily Solovyov-Sedoy. It was later covered as "Midnight in Moscow" by Kenny Ball.

title: “Sheila” by Tommy Roe
text: "Sheila" is a song written and recorded by Tommy Roe. The single reached number one on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 on September 1, 1962, remaining in the top position for two weeks and peaking at number six on the US Billboard R&B chart.

title: “Twistin' the Night Away” by Sam Cooke
text: "Twistin' the Night Away" is a song written and recorded by Sam Cooke. It was recorded on 18 December 1961 and released as a single in 1962.
listen: Twistin' the Night Away Sam Cooke

title: “The Wah-Watusi” by The Orlons
text: "The Wah-Watusi" is a song written by Kal Mann and Dave Appell and recorded by the Orlons in 1962. It is named for the Watusi, a popular dance style among American teenagers during the early 1960s.

title: “Peppermint Twist” by Joey Dee and the Starliters
text: "Peppermint Twist" is a song written by Joey Dee and Henry Glover, recorded and released by Joey Dee and the Starliters in 1961. Capitalizing on the Twist dance craze and the nightclub in which Dee performed, the song hit No.1 on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 in early 1962.
listen: Peppermint Twist Joey Dee and the Starliters

title: “Break It to Me Gently” by Brenda Lee
text: "Break It to Me Gently" is a pop song written by blues musician Joe Seneca with lyrics by Diane Lampert. Both Brenda Lee and Juice Newton were met with considerable success with their versions of the song.
listen: Break It to Me Gently Brenda Lee

title: “Having a Party” by Sam Cooke
text: "Having a Party" is a song by American singer-songwriter Sam Cooke, released on May 8, 1962, by RCA Victor. Produced by Hugo & Luigi and arranged and conducted by René Hall, the song was the A-side to "Bring It On Home to Me".

title: “Green Onions” by Booker T. & the M.G.'s
text: "Green Onions" is an instrumental composition recorded in 1962 by Booker T. & the M.G.'s. One of the most popular rock and soul songs, and one of the best-known R&B instrumentals of its era, it utilizes a twelve-bar blues progression and features a rippling Hammond M3 organ line played by frontman Booker T. Jones, who created it when he was 17 by improvising in the studio.
listen: Green Onions Booker T. & the M.G.'s

title: “You Don't Know Me” by Ray Charles
text: "You Don't Know Me" is a song written by Eddy Arnold and Cindy Walker in 1955. It was first recorded by Arnold that year and released as a single on April 21, 1956, on RCA Victor.
wiki: You Don't Know Me (Cindy Walker song)
listen: You Don't Know Me Ray Charles

title: “Sherry” by The Four Seasons
text: "Sherry" is a song written by Bob Gaudio and recorded by the Four Seasons.

title: 1962 NHRA Winternationals: Carol Cox becomes the first woman allowed to race at a National Hot Rod Association national event in the United States; she wins in the Super Stock class.
text: The 1962 NHRA Winternationals were a National Hot Rod Association drag racing event, held at Auto Club Raceway, Pomona, California on 18 February.

title: Project Mercury: Aboard Friendship 7, John Glenn becomes the first American to orbit the Earth, three times in 4 hours, 55 minutes.
text: Mercury-Atlas 6 was the first crewed American orbital spaceflight, which took place on February 20, 1962. Piloted by astronaut John Glenn and operated by NASA as part of Project Mercury, it was the fifth human spaceflight, preceded by Soviet orbital flights Vostok 1 and 2 and American sub-orbital flights Mercury-Redstone 3 and 4.

title: March–May – Yi–Ta incident: At least 60,000 Chinese citizens migrate from the People's Republic of China to the Soviet Union, predominantly (but not exclusively) ethnic Kazakhs.
text: The Yi–Ta incident was a mass exodus of people from China to the Soviet Union in early 1962. At least 60,000 Chinese citizens migrated to the Soviet Union by crossing the border between the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region and the Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic from March to May 1962.

title: American Airlines Flight 1 (a Boeing 707) crashes on takeoff at New York International Airport, after a rudder malfunction causes an uncontrolled roll, resulting in the loss of control of the aircraft, with the loss of all 95 on board.
text: The Boeing 707 is an early American long-range narrow-body airliner, the first jetliner developed and produced by Boeing Commercial Airplanes. Developed from the Boeing 367-80 prototype, the initial 707-120 first flew on December 20, 1957.

title: A military coup in Burma brings General Ne Win to power.
text: Ne Win was a Burmese general and politician who served as Burma's head of government from 1958 to 1960 and again from 1962 to 1974; and also as head of state from 1962 to 1981. Ne Win was Burma's military dictator during the Socialist Republic of the Union of Burma period of 1962 to 1988.

title: Katangan Prime Minister Moise Tshombe begins negotiations to rejoin the Congo.
text: Moïse Kapenda Tshombe was a Congolese businessman and politician. He served as the president of the secessionist State of Katanga from 1960 to 1963 and as prime minister of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1964 to 1965.

title: Flying Tiger Line Flight 739, a Lockheed L-1049H Super Constellation chartered by the United States Military Air Transport Service, and carrying mainly United States Army personnel bound for South Vietnam, vanishes over the western Pacific…
text: Flying Tiger Line Flight 739 was a Lockheed L-1049 Super Constellation propliner that disappeared on March 16, 1962, over the western Pacific Ocean. The aircraft, which had been chartered by the United States Army, was transporting ninety-six military passengers from Travis Air Force Base in California to Tan Son Nhat International Airport in Saigon, South Vietnam.

title: Évian Accords: France and Algeria sign an agreement in Évian-les-Bains, ending the Algerian War.
text: The Évian Accords were a set of declarations between the French Government and the Provisional Government of the Algerian Republic on 18 March 1962 in Évian-les-Bains which outlined the agreements for Algeria's Independence alongside cooperation with France. The Accords consisted of five chapters which detailed the guarantees and principals of this Independence.

title: "Un premier amour", sung by Isabelle Aubret (music by Claude-Henri Vic, lyrics by Roland Stephane Valade), wins the Eurovision Song Contest 1962 (staged in Luxembourg) for France.
text: Isabelle Aubret is a French singer best known for winning the Eurovision Song Contest in 1962 with the song "Un premier amour".

title: An armistice begins in Algeria; however, the OAS continues its terrorist attacks against Algerians.
text: An armistice is a formal agreement of conflicting parties to stop fighting. It is not necessarily the end of a war, as it may constitute only a cessation of hostilities while an attempt is made to negotiate a lasting peace.

title: The Scandinavian States of the Nordic Council sign the Helsinki Convention on Nordic Co-operation.
text: The Nordic Council is the official body for formal inter-parliamentary Nordic cooperation among the Nordic countries. Formed in 1952, it has 87 representatives from Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden, as well as from the autonomous areas of the Faroe Islands, Greenland, and Åland.

title: OAS leader Edmond Jouhaud is arrested in Oran.
text: Edmond Jules René Jouhaud was one of four French generals who briefly staged a putsch in Algeria in April 1961.

title: France shortens the term for military service from 26 months to 18.
text: Conscription, also known as the draft in American and Philippine English, is the practice in which the compulsory enlistment in a national service, mainly a military service, is enforced by law. Conscription dates back to antiquity and it continues in some countries to the present day under various names.

title: Jawaharlal Nehru is elected de facto Prime Minister of India, for the fourth time.
text: Jawaharlal Nehru was an Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, secular humanist, social democrat, and statesman who was a central figure in India during the middle of the 20th century. Nehru was a principal leader of the Indian nationalist movement in the 1930s and 1940s.

title: Belgium reestablishes diplomatic relations with the Congo.
text: Diplomacy is the communication by representatives of state, intergovernmental, or non-governmental institutions intended to influence events in the international system. Diplomacy is the main instrument of foreign policy which represents the broader goals and strategies that guide a state's interactions with the rest of the world.

title: Milovan Đilas, author and former vice-president of Yugoslavia is re-arrested.
text: Milovan Djilas was a Yugoslav communist politician, theorist and author. He was a key figure in the Partisan movement during World War II, as well as in the post-war government.
